```yaml
      case "$(uname -m)" in
        x86_64)
          jq_asset=jq-linux-amd64
          jq_sha256=5942c9b0934e510ee61eb3e30273f1b3fe2590df93933a93d7c58b81d19c8ff5
          ;;
        aarch64|arm64)
          jq_asset=jq-linux-arm64
          jq_sha256=4dd2d8a0661df0b22f1bb9a1f9830f06b6f3b8f7d91211a1ef5d7c4f06a8b4a5
          ;;
        *)
          echo "unsupported jq runner architecture: $(uname -m)" >&2
          exit 1
          ;;
      esac
      curl -fsSL "https://github.com/jqlang/jq/releases/download/jq-1.7.1/${jq_asset}" -o "$jq_path"
      echo "${jq_sha256}  ${jq_path}" | sha256sum -c -
      chmod 0755 "$jq_path"
      "$jq_path" --version
      echo "$tool_dir" >> "$RWX_ENV/PATH"

  # No packaged `uv/install` leaf exists in the RWX catalog (verified via
  # `rwx packages list` 2026-10-03 -- `python/install` installs Python, not
  # uv), so this manual installer stays. Checksum-pinned so an altered or
  # compromised script at that URL fails closed instead of executing -- same
  # pattern as gtm-sdk's .rwx/trunk-check.yml uv-install task.
  # The source workflow's astral-sh/setup-uv resolved the latest uv (it pins
  # only the action, not uv); this port pins 0.11.29 instead -- the version
  # the exact steps below were validated against (uv sync --locked + full
  # pytest suite). Unlike gtm-sdk, this repo's pyproject.toml carries no
  # [tool.uv] required-version pin, so bumping this is safe as long as the
  # committed uv.lock still parses and `uv sync --locked` stays clean.
  - key: uv-install
    use: [jq-install]
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      script="$(mktemp)"
      trap 'rm -f "${script}"' EXIT
      curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/0.11.29/install.sh -o "${script}"
      echo "504a79fd2ed0dcd47e7f04f0792cfd0871f62e24a7fe40fa8ae0f563a369f2bd  ${script}" | sha256sum -c -
      sh "${script}"
      echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$RWX_ENV/PATH"

  # No `filter:` here -- `uv sync` installs gtm-linear editable and the test
  # suite imports scripts/ and operations/ too, so the full source tree must
  # be present (same rationale as gtm-sdk's .rwx/trunk-check.yml deps task).
  # UV_LOCKED and UV_PYTHON are exported to $RWX_ENV so every downstream
  # `uv run` inherits them -- the RWX equivalent of the source workflow's
  # workflow-level `env:` block, which existed so `uv run` steps fail loudly
  # on lockfile drift instead of silently re-resolving off PyPI. UV_PYTHON
  # mirrors setup-uv's python-version input (which sets UV_PYTHON).
  - key: deps
    use: [uv-install]
    env:
      UV_LOCKED: "1"
      UV_PYTHON: "3.13"
    run: |
      uv sync
      echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$RWX_ENV/PATH"
      echo "$PWD/.venv" > "$RWX_ENV/VIRTUAL_ENV"
      echo "1" > "$RWX_ENV/UV_LOCKED"
      echo "3.13" > "$RWX_ENV/UV_PYTHON"

  - key: captain
    call: rwx/install-captain 1.2.0

  # Ports the source workflow's `test` job (Tests / Operations are current /
  # Generated code is current), split in three so failing and flaky runs still
  # reach Trunk: `pytest` records pytest's exit code instead of failing,
  # `trunk-upload` uploads the JUnit files, and `test` re-fails on the saved
  # code, then runs the two --check scripts in the original order.
  - key: pytest
    use: [deps, captain]
    env:
      REQUIRE_JQ: "1"
    run: |
      mkdir -p tmp
      set +e
      captain run sdk-python-linear-pytest
      echo "$?" > tmp/pytest-exit-code

  # Uploads to Trunk Flaky Tests. TRUNK_API_TOKEN is the org-wide Trunk API
  # token (the Analytics CLI accepts no scoped key), so it lives in its own
  # `sdk-python-linear-trunk` vault -- never in `sdk-python-linear`, which holds
  # GITHUB_TOKEN and PYPI_TOKEN. Access model: locked, grants
  # `elviskahoro/sdk-python-linear:**`, `*/*`, and `:main`, approvals disabled,
  # same reasoning as `sdk-python-linear-it` (see integration-tests.yml).
  # Branch patterns do not cross `/` (measured on #192/#193), so `*/*` is what
  # lets slashed PR branches (`conductor/...`, `w-565/...`) resolve the token;
  # with only `**` and `:main` every owner PR leg fast-fails before `run:`.
  # Never add another secret to it. The `if:` is the only author gate (vault
  # grants match repo + ref, never author) and is evaluated before `env:`
  # resolves the secret, so skipped PRs (forks, other authors) never touch the
  # vault; an unresolvable secret would otherwise fail the task before `run:`.
  # cache: false + cache-key: excluded keep the token out of the content-cache
  # fingerprint and make every run actually upload. RWX is not a CI provider
  # Trunk auto-detects, so CUSTOM=true plus the job/branch/PR variables
  # attribute the run. Captain's retry command writes a separate -retry.xml
  # (see .captain/config.yml); the glob uploads both. The launcher download is
  # pinned to the same fail-closed checksum as .rwx/lint.yml's trunk-install
  # task (trunk.io/releases/trunk is latest-only -- no versioned URL exists),
  # the CLI reads the token from its TRUNK_API_TOKEN env default instead of a
  # --token flag so it never appears in the process list, and `< /dev/null`
  # guards against the interactive-prompt hang .rwx/lint.yml documents for
  # trunk in TTY-less CI.
  - key: trunk-upload
    use: [pytest]
    if: ${{ init.event-type != 'pull_request' || init.pr-author == 'elviskahoro' }}
    cache: false
    env:
      TRUNK_API_TOKEN:
        value: ${{ vaults.sdk-python-linear-trunk.secrets.TRUNK_API_TOKEN }}
        cache-key: excluded
      TRUNK_ORG_SLUG: sanhedrin
      TRUNK_TEST_COLLECTION_ID: HJL9OODn
      CUSTOM: "true"
      JOB_URL: https://cloud.rwx.com/mint/elviskahoro/runs/${{ run.id }}
      BRANCH: ${{ init.branch }}
      PR_NUMBER: ${{ init.pr-number }}
      COMMIT_BRANCH: ${{ init.branch }}
      COMMIT_SHA: ${{ init.commit-sha }}
      REPO: ${{ init.repository }}
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      trunk_launcher="$(mktemp)"
      if ! curl -fsSL https://trunk.io/releases/trunk -o "${trunk_launcher}" ||
        ! echo "700f8bbedfd226595999ea2202b9a7af75ba8398dd711f5f159f5bbba6cbf322  ${trunk_launcher}" | sha256sum -c -; then
        rm -f "${trunk_launcher}"
        echo "error: trunk launcher download or checksum failed" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      chmod 0755 "${trunk_launcher}"
      # The workspace has no .git (git/clone leaves none), so the repo
      # identity is passed explicitly (--use-uncloned-repo). Three layers keep
      # a run that uploaded nothing from going green: the CLI's own nonzero
      # exit (pipefail carries it through tee) for errored uploads, the grep
      # for its error banner in case a class of error still exits 0 under its
      # quarantining exit code, and --allow-empty-test-results=false for a
      # glob that matches no JUnit files. --pr-number is only valid when
      # non-empty (push legs set it to "").
      upload_log="$(mktemp)"
      pr_args=()
      if [ -n "${PR_NUMBER}" ]; then
        pr_args=(--pr-number "${PR_NUMBER}")
      fi
      "${trunk_launcher}" flakytests upload \
        --junit-paths "tmp/junit-*.xml" \
        --allow-empty-test-results=false \
        --org-url-slug "${TRUNK_ORG_SLUG}" \
        --use-uncloned-repo \
        --repo-url "${REPO}" \
        --repo-head-sha "${COMMIT_SHA}" \
        --repo-head-branch "${BRANCH}" \
        --repo-head-author-name rwx \
        --repo-head-commit-epoch "$(date +%s)" \
        "${pr_args[@]}" < /dev/null 2>&1 | tee "${upload_log}"
      if grep -q "Error Encountered" "${upload_log}"; then
        echo "error: trunk upload reported an error" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      rm -f "${trunk_launcher}" "${upload_log}"

  # `after` is an expression, not a list: a list-form `after:` only runs the
  # task when every listed task *succeeds*, and a skipped task is not a
  # succeeded one (https://www.rwx.com/docs/after), so `after: [trunk-upload]`
  # would skip `test` on every non-owner PR leg -- a green required status
  # with no pytest run. `succeeded || skipped` keeps the upload ordered on
  # legs that run it and still gates every PR leg on the suite; a failed
  # upload (e.g. unresolvable vault) skips `test` and reddens the run there.
  - key: test
    use: [pytest]
    after: ${{ trunk-upload.succeeded || trunk-upload.skipped }}
    run: |
      code="$(cat tmp/pytest-exit-code)"
      if [ "${code}" != "0" ]; then
        echo "pytest failed (exit ${code})" >&2
        exit "${code}"
      fi
      # Fails if operations/*.graphql drifted from operations/_spec.toml.
      uv run python scripts/gen_operations.py --check
      # Fails if a generated model was hand-edited or the schema pin moved
      # without regenerating.
      uv run python scripts/codegen.py --check

  # Ports the source workflow's `lean-install` job: the wheel must build and
  # import with only its runtime deps. `use:`s [uv-install] rather than
  # [deps] to mirror the source job, which never runs uv sync -- `uv build`
  # builds in an isolated hatchling env, and the import check installs only
  # dist/*.whl into a throwaway venv.
  - key: lean-install
    use: [uv-install]
    env:
      UV_PYTHON: "3.13"
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      uv build
      uv venv -p 3.13 /tmp/lean
      VIRTUAL_ENV=/tmp/lean uv pip install dist/*.whl
      # Capture the listing before grepping it: under `set -o pipefail`,
      # `grep -q` exits on first match and uv can take SIGPIPE (141), which
      # would make the `if` false and pass the guard exactly when the leak
      # exists. Captured-then-grepped closes that fail-open window.
      lean_list="$(VIRTUAL_ENV=/tmp/lean uv pip list)"
      if grep -qi strawberry <<<"${lean_list}"; then
        echo "strawberry leaked into the runtime dependency tree"; exit 1
      fi
      /tmp/lean/bin/python -c "import gtm_linear; print(gtm_linear.__version__)"

  # Ports the source workflow's `schema-drift` job (originally schedule-only;
  # now runs on every trigger): network-marked tests are deselected by
  # default; this task runs them so upstream drift surfaces in CI rather
  # than in a user's traceback. Keyless by design -- no trigger needs vault
  # access to stay green: the schema test fetches Linear's public SDK schema
  # from raw.githubusercontent.com; the live-API wording check self-skips
  # without LINEAR_API_KEY (the vault key lives in `sdk-python-linear-it` and is
  # injected only by the integration-tests.yml pipeline, whose PR trigger is
  # author-gated); and
  # tests/integration's bad-key check runs keyless against api.linear.app,
  # since an invalid key must still surface AUTHENTICATION_ERROR. That last
  # call does make PR-run greenness depend on api.linear.app being reachable
  # and honoring its auth-error contract -- deliberate: it pins the exact
  # failure a user with a bad key sees.
  # cache: false is required, not cosmetic: the result depends on Linear's
  # live schema, not just this repo's files, so a cache hit would freeze the
  # drift check exactly when upstream moved. RWX caches tasks by content by
  # default and does not detect non-determinism (see
  # https://www.rwx.com/docs/caching).
  - key: schema-drift
    use: [deps, captain]
    cache: false
    run: captain run sdk-python-linear-pytest-network
```

### Gotchas visible in the reference files
- **Triggers:** `on.github` takes `pull_request`, `push` (a single item or a list of `- if:` items) and `status-checks: name:`. `on.cli`, `on.dispatch` and `on.cron` are also available. A manual run needs a `cli` entry.
- **Merge-queue branches:** the queue's `trunk-merge/**` branches are matched with `starts-with(event.git.branch, 'trunk-merge/')`.
- **Base image:** all files use `base: image: ubuntu:24.04` with `config: rwx/base 1.2.0`. Standard tasks are `git/clone 2.2.0`, `python/install 2.0.1`, `rwx/install-captain 1.2.0` and `github/install-cli 1.1.0`.
- **PATH:** later tasks pick up tools through `echo … >> "$RWX_ENV/PATH"`.
- **Cache keys:** `filter:` applies only to the task that defines it. Anything depending on external state needs `cache: false`. Secrets use `cache-key: excluded`.
- **`after:`:** use `after: ${{ x.succeeded || x.skipped }}`. A list form silently skips gates when an upstream task is skipped.
- **Vaults:** branch globs do not cross `/`, so grants need both `**` and `*/*`. The "Allow public repositories" toggle is UI-only.
- **Repo visibility:** both reference repos are public, so `git/clone` needs no token.

This is the CI/CD inventory for buridan-ui, plus the RWX reference pattern from `sdk-python-attio` and `sdk-python-linear`. Nothing was modified. The sibling `.rwx/*.yml` files are quoted verbatim below. Four of them (`spec-update-check.yml`, the Linear `dagger-ref-drift.yml`, the Linear `.migration-inventory.md` and the Linear `publish.yml` header) were not fully read, and I did not open the 11 non-`.rwx` references in the Attio and Linear trunk and `AGENTS.md` files.

## 1. buridan-ui: current CI/CD state

**Branch and RWX status.**
- The checked-out branch is `conductor/rwx-ci-cd-migration`. It sits at `ebce196`, which is also `origin/main`. It has no commits of its own and a clean tree, so no migration work has started.
- There is no `.rwx/` directory and no RWX reference anywhere in the working tree.
- `git grep -i rwx` on HEAD finds only `reflex.lock/bun.lock`, which is an unrelated hash match. The only RWX mention is in `.github/workflows/trunk-check.yml`: "gtm-sdk's lint pipeline does the same (its .rwx/trunk-check.yml deps task runs uv sync before checks)".
- Git history has no `.rwx` files. The `-S'.rwx'` hits are `10bbb3d`, `ea7f891` and `b1cbb69`, the "Trunk Merge Queue setup (#124)" commits, which carry that same comment line.
- Relevant history:
  - `10bbb3d` (#124) added the trunk merge-queue CI gates.
  - `71dbe68` (#230) added the impacted-targets upload.
  - `e98abdf` (#232) switched Pullfrog to glm-5p3-flash.
  - `8ae83f8` (#59) and `6f52201` (#46) set up Pullfrog.
  - `9a4abb1` (#84) added the docs-and-assets validation workflow.
  - Older commits ("update deploy github workflow", `e0b2329`, `ac24fb3`, `265182d`) show a former deploy workflow that no longer exists.
- Local `main` (`5c89bf2`) is stale relative to `origin/main`. `git rev-parse` also printed a promisor/corruption warning about `ebce196` being missing from the object store. Treat `git diff main` as unreliable and compare against `origin/main`.

**Absent entirely:**
- `.github/actions`
- dependabot or renovate config
- Makefile
- Dockerfile
- `vercel.json`
- `.pre-commit-config`
- any Reflex Cloud or Vercel deploy config

`.github/FUNDING.yml` only holds `github: [LineIndent]`. `rxconfig.py` is app config only and has no deploy block. `reflex-hosting-cli` is a dev dependency, but nothing invokes it. The old deploy workflow is gone.

### Workflows (`/home/vercel-sandbox/buridan-ui/.github/workflows/`)

All five declare `permissions: contents: read` at workflow level.

**1. `tests.yml` (workflow "Tests", job `tests`, check name "Tests")**
- Triggers: `push` on `main` and `trunk-merge/**`, and `pull_request` on `main`.
- Runs on `ubuntu-latest`.
- Steps:
  1. `actions/checkout@3d3c42e5… # v7.0.1`
  2. `astral-sh/setup-uv@1c37ad07… # v10.3.0` (caching on by default)
  3. `uv sync --frozen --group dev`
  4. `uv run pytest -q`
- It uses no secrets or env.

**2. `trunk-check.yml` (workflow "Trunk Check", job `trunk-check`, check name "Trunk Check")**
- Triggers: `push` on `trunk-merge/**` only, and `pull_request` on `main`. There is deliberately no push-to-main run.
- Steps:
  1. Checkout with `fetch-depth: 0`.
  2. `setup-uv`, then `uv sync --frozen --group dev`. This is needed because pyrefly and pyright resolve against `.venv`.
  3. Install the trunk launcher, checksum-pinned. It runs `curl -fsSL https://trunk.io/releases/trunk`, verifies `sha256 700f8bbe…f322`, then runs `sudo install -m 755 … /usr/local/bin/trunk`.
  4. For `pull_request` events:
     - If `GITHUB_REF == refs/pull/$PR_NUMBER/merge`, set `upstream=$(git rev-parse HEAD^1)`.
     - Otherwise set `upstream=$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)`.
     - Then run `trunk check --upstream="$upstream" --ci < /dev/null`.
  5. For `push` events: `trunk check --upstream="$(git rev-parse HEAD^1)" --ci < /dev/null`.
- Env: `PR_NUMBER` comes from `github.event.pull_request.number`. No secrets.

**3. `validate-assets.yml` (workflow "Docs & Assets", job `validate-generated-assets`, check name "Generate & Verify Docs and Social Cards")**
- Triggers: `push` on `main` and `trunk-merge/**`, and `pull_request` on `main`.
- Steps:
  1. Checkout `3d3c42e5… v7.0.1`.
  2. `actions/setup-python@5fda3b95… v7.0.0` with Python 3.12.
  3. `pip install uv`
  4. `uv sync --group dev` (not `--frozen`)
  5. `uv run python scripts/generate_anatomy.py --check`
  6. `uv run python scripts/generate_markdown.py`
  7. `git diff --exit-code assets/docs`
  8. `uv run pytest tests/test_generated_assets.py tests/test_toc_scrollspy.py`

**4. `trunk-impacted-targets.yml` (workflow "Trunk Impacted Targets", job `upload-impacted-targets`, "Upload Impacted Targets")**

**5. `pullfrog.yml` (workflow "Pullfrog")**
- Trigger: `workflow_dispatch` only, with inputs `prompt` and `name`. The header says it is vendor-managed: "DO NOT EDIT EXCEPT WHERE INDICATED".
- Permissions are `id-token: write` and `contents: read`.
- Steps:
  1. Checkout `d23441a4… v6.1.0` with `fetch-depth: 1`.
  2. `pullfrog/pullfrog@ad4283a8… v0.1.98` with `model: fireworks-ai/accounts/fireworks/models/glm-5p3-flash`.
- Secrets passed as env: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `FIREWORKS_API_KEY`, `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `XAI_API_KEY`, `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, `MOONSHOT_API_KEY`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `OPENCODE_API_KEY`. Bedrock, Vertex, Azure and OpenAI-compatible variables are commented out.
- `.trunk/trunk.yaml` has a checkov ignore for this file.

### Trunk and merge queue (`.trunk/trunk.yaml`)

  - Attio: `"RWX: trunk-check"`, `"RWX: pytest"`.
  - Without `status-checks.name`, the RWX status name is `RWX: <file>.yml (pull request)`. With `status-checks: name: X`, it is `RWX: X`.

### Verbatim: `/home/vercel-sandbox/sdk-python-attio/.rwx/trunk-check.yml`
```yaml
# Trunk lint gate (diff-only) for the Trunk Merge Queue.
# Not path-filtered: a path-filtered required check does not report on
# every PR and would deadlock the Trunk Merge Queue. PR and queue/main pushes
# share one status-check name so a single check covers both.
on:
  github:
    pull_request:
      init:
        commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
        lint-upstream: origin/main
      status-checks:
        name: trunk-check
    push:
      - if: ${{ event.git.branch == 'main' }}
        init:
          commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
          lint-upstream: HEAD^
        status-checks:
          name: trunk-check
      - if: ${{ starts-with(event.git.branch, 'trunk-merge/') || starts-with(event.git.branch, 'trunk-merge-beta/') }}
        init:
          commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
          lint-upstream: origin/main
        status-checks:
          name: trunk-check
  cli:
    init:
      commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
      lint-upstream: origin/main

base:
  image: ubuntu:24.04
  config: rwx/base 1.2.0

tasks:
  - key: code
    call: git/clone 2.2.0
    with:
      repository: https://github.com/elviskahoro/sdk-python-attio.git
      ref: ${{ init.commit-sha }}
      preserve-git-dir: true
      fetch-full-depth: true

  - key: python
    call: python/install 2.0.1
    with:
      python-version: "3.13"

  - key: uv
    use: python
    run: pip install uv

  - key: sync
    use: [code, uv]
    run: uv sync
    filter:
      - pyproject.toml
      - uv.lock

  # Trunk launcher, checksum-pinned: trunk.io/releases/trunk is latest-only,
  # so the bytes are pinned and any upstream change fails closed (same pin as
  # .rwx/pytest.yml). Re-pin deliberately if the checksum no longer matches.
  - key: trunk-install
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      trunk_launcher="$(mktemp)"
      if ! curl -fsSL https://trunk.io/releases/trunk -o "${trunk_launcher}" ||
        ! echo "700f8bbedfd226595999ea2202b9a7af75ba8398dd711f5f159f5bbba6cbf322  ${trunk_launcher}" | sha256sum -c -; then
        rm -f "${trunk_launcher}"
        echo "error: trunk launcher download or checksum failed" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      if ! install -m 755 "${trunk_launcher}" /usr/local/bin/trunk 2>/dev/null; then
        mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
        install -m 755 "${trunk_launcher}" "$HOME/.local/bin/trunk"
        echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$RWX_ENV/PATH"
      fi
      rm -f "${trunk_launcher}"

  # Tool cache. A `filter` scopes only the task that defines it: downstream
  # `use:`rs do NOT inherit it and cache-key on every workspace file, so
  # trunk-config and trunk-tools each declare the same .trunk/ filter and
  # both are load-bearing. trunk-config keys on .trunk/ alone, freezing the
  # $HOME/trunk-seed bytes it writes (outside-workspace files are always
  # keyed, never filtered); trunk-tools keys on .trunk/ plus the pinned
  # launcher. Every linter, runtime and plugin pin is downloaded once and
  # reused until trunk.yaml changes. Keep the two filter lists in lockstep.
  - key: trunk-config
    use: code
    filter:
      - .trunk/trunk.yaml
      - .trunk/configs
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      mkdir -p "$HOME/trunk-seed"
      cp -r .trunk "$HOME/trunk-seed/.trunk"
      rm -rf "$HOME/trunk-seed/.trunk/.gitignore"
      cd "$HOME/trunk-seed"
      git init -q
      # Pin the dates so a cold-cache re-execution writes identical bytes
      # instead of busting trunk-tools' key with wall-clock timestamps.
      export GIT_AUTHOR_DATE="2000-01-01T00:00:00+00:00"
      export GIT_COMMITTER_DATE="2000-01-01T00:00:00+00:00"
      git -c user.name=rwx -c user.email=rwx@example.com commit -q --allow-empty -m seed

  - key: trunk-tools
    use: [trunk-install, trunk-config]
    filter:
      - .trunk/trunk.yaml
      - .trunk/configs
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      cd "$HOME/trunk-seed"
      trunk install --ci < /dev/null

  - key: lint
    use: [sync, trunk-tools]
    env:
      UPSTREAM: ${{ init.lint-upstream }}
    run: |
      # Lint only the diff, like trunk-action. The trigger picks the base
      # (PR/queue: main, push to main: previous commit) rather than this
      # script inferring it from the branch name, which a fork PR from its
      # own `main` would spoof.
      if [ "$UPSTREAM" = "origin/main" ]; then
        git fetch origin main
      fi
      trunk check --ci --upstream "$UPSTREAM"
```

```yaml
          event-type: push
          pr-author: ""
          pr-number: ""
        status-checks:
          name: pytest
  cli:
    init:
      commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
      branch: ${{ event.git.branch }}
      repository: https://github.com/elviskahoro/sdk-python-attio.git
      event-type: push
      pr-author: ""
      pr-number: ""

base:
  image: ubuntu:24.04
  config: rwx/base 1.2.0

tasks:
  - key: code
    call: git/clone 2.2.0
    with:
      repository: https://github.com/elviskahoro/sdk-python-attio.git
      ref: ${{ init.commit-sha }}
      preserve-git-dir: true
      fetch-full-depth: true

  - key: python
    call: python/install 2.0.1
    with:
      python-version: "3.13"

  - key: uv
    use: python
    run: pip install uv

  - key: sync
    use: [code, uv]
    run: uv sync
    # The project installs editable from generated/src, so the sources must be
    # in the workspace or `import attio` fails on a fresh (uncached) sync.
    filter:
      - pyproject.toml
      - uv.lock
      - README.md
      - generated/src
      - attio_cli

  - key: captain
    call: rwx/install-captain 1.2.0

  # Split in three so failing and flaky runs still reach Trunk: `pytest-run`
  # records captain's exit code instead of failing, `trunk-upload` uploads the
  # JUnit files, and `pytest` re-fails on the saved code.
  - key: pytest-run
    use: [sync, captain]
    # Uncached: captain run uploads test insights and reads cloud-side
    # quarantines at run time; a cache hit on a same-commit re-run (PR
    # reopen, rwx retry) would replay the recorded output and skip both,
    # so a quarantine granted after the original run never applies.
    cache: false
    run: |
      mkdir -p tmp
      set +e
      captain run sdk-python-attio-pytest
      echo "$?" > tmp/pytest-exit-code

  # Uploads to Trunk Flaky Tests. TRUNK_API_TOKEN is the org-wide Trunk API
  # token (the Analytics CLI accepts no scoped key), so it lives in its own
  # `sdk-python-attio-trunk` vault; never add another secret to it. The `if:`
  # is the only author gate (vault grants match repo + ref, never author).
  # RWX documents no ordering between a task's `if:` and its `env:` secret
  # resolution, so whether a skipped task touches the vault is unverifiable;
  # what holds regardless: a skipped task never executes its script, so the
  # token cannot reach code on skipped legs (and fork PRs never run at all).
  # Vault grants must include `elviskahoro/sdk-python-attio:**`, `*/*` and
  # `:main` (branch patterns do not cross `/`); the repository scope of the
  # repo-less grants is undocumented, so only `rwx vaults list` can confirm
  # whether `*/*` reaches other org repos. cache: false + cache-key: excluded
  # keep the token out of the content-cache fingerprint and make every run
  # actually upload. RWX is not a CI provider Trunk auto-detects, so
  # CUSTOM=true plus the job/branch/PR variables attribute the run. Captain's
  # retry command writes a separate -retry.xml (see .captain/config.yml); the
  # glob uploads both. The launcher sha256 pins only the bash bootstrap
  # (trunk.io/releases/trunk is latest-only); TRUNK_ANALYTICS_CLI_VERSION
  # pins the trunk-analytics-cli binary that the bootstrap downloads and
  # runs. The launcher verifies no tarball digest either way, so that version
  # pin is the only control on the executed CLI (the lint gate pins its CLI
  # the same way, `cli.version` in .trunk/trunk.yaml). Bump the checksum and
  # the version deliberately.
  - key: trunk-upload
    use: [pytest-run]
    if: ${{ init.event-type != 'pull_request' || init.pr-author == 'elviskahoro' }}
    cache: false
    env:
      TRUNK_API_TOKEN:
        value: ${{ vaults.sdk-python-attio-trunk.secrets.TRUNK_API_TOKEN }}
        cache-key: excluded
      TRUNK_ORG_SLUG: sanhedrin
      TRUNK_TEST_COLLECTION_ID: xw7SIPox
      # Bare semver (no `v` prefix); the launcher rejects non-semver values.
      TRUNK_ANALYTICS_CLI_VERSION: "0.16.1"
      CUSTOM: "true"
      BRANCH: ${{ init.branch }}
      PR_NUMBER: ${{ init.pr-number }}
      COMMIT_BRANCH: ${{ init.branch }}
      COMMIT_SHA: ${{ init.commit-sha }}
      REPO: ${{ init.repository }}
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      # RWX auto-exposes RWX_RUN_URL (www.rwx.com/docs/environment-variables).
      export JOB_URL="${RWX_RUN_URL}"
      trunk_launcher="$(mktemp)"
      if ! curl -fsSL https://trunk.io/releases/trunk -o "${trunk_launcher}" ||
        ! echo "700f8bbedfd226595999ea2202b9a7af75ba8398dd711f5f159f5bbba6cbf322  ${trunk_launcher}" | sha256sum -c -; then
        rm -f "${trunk_launcher}"
        echo "error: trunk launcher download or checksum failed" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      chmod 0755 "${trunk_launcher}"
      # Guard against a run that uploaded nothing going green: pipefail
      # carries the CLI's exit code through tee, the grep catches its error
      # banner under the quarantining exit code, and
      # --allow-empty-test-results=false catches a glob matching no files.
      # --pr-number is only valid when non-empty (push legs set it to "").
      upload_log="$(mktemp)"
      pr_args=()
      if [ -n "${PR_NUMBER}" ]; then
        pr_args=(--pr-number "${PR_NUMBER}")
      fi
      # The head commit's time, not upload time, so reruns of old commits
      # keep Trunk's history ordered; fall back if the checkout lacks it.
      commit_epoch="$(git show -s --format=%ct "${COMMIT_SHA}" 2>/dev/null || date +%s)"
      "${trunk_launcher}" flakytests upload \
        --junit-paths "tmp/junit-*.xml" \
        --allow-empty-test-results=false \
        --org-url-slug "${TRUNK_ORG_SLUG}" \
        --use-uncloned-repo \
        --repo-url "${REPO}" \
        --repo-head-sha "${COMMIT_SHA}" \
        --repo-head-branch "${BRANCH}" \
        --repo-head-author-name rwx \
        --repo-head-commit-epoch "${commit_epoch}" \
        "${pr_args[@]}" < /dev/null 2>&1 | tee "${upload_log}"
      if grep -q "Error Encountered" "${upload_log}"; then
        echo "error: trunk upload reported an error" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      rm -f "${trunk_launcher}" "${upload_log}"

  # `after` is an expression, not a list: a list-form `after:` skips the task
  # when a listed task is skipped (https://www.rwx.com/docs/after), which
  # would hand non-owner PR legs a green required status without a pytest
  # verdict. This gate re-fails on the exit code saved by `pytest-run`.
  - key: pytest
    use: [pytest-run]
    after: ${{ trunk-upload.succeeded || trunk-upload.skipped }}
    run: exit "$(cat tmp/pytest-exit-code)"
```

```yaml
  image: ubuntu:24.04
  config: rwx/base 1.2.0

      ref: ${{ init.commit-sha }}

      # PR's base commit (git cat-file + fetch + merge-base) and diffs against it via
      # `trunk check --upstream` -- both need real git history, not a
      # shallow snapshot (same reason gtm-sdk's trunk-check code task sets
      # these flags, unlike this repo's tests.yml clone, which nothing
      # history-dependent consumes). Public repo, so no github-token is
      # needed.
      fetch-full-depth: true
      preserve-git-dir: true

  # rationale there: the astral.sh script at a versioned URL is stable for
  # that version, and pinning the bytes makes an altered or compromised
  # script fail closed instead of executing. Version matches tests.yml's
  # (validated against uv sync --locked + the full pytest suite).
  - key: uv-install
    use: [code]

      set -euo pipefail
      script="$(mktemp)"
      trap 'rm -f "${script}"' EXIT

  - key: trunk-install

  # `filter` scopes only the task that defines it: downstream `use:`rs do
  # NOT inherit it and cache-key on every workspace file
  # (rwx.com/docs/filtering-files, "Sharing filters across tasks") -- so
  # trunk-config and trunk-tools each declare the same .trunk/ filter, and
  # both are load-bearing. trunk-config's keys its own cache on .trunk/
  # alone, freezing the $HOME/trunk-seed bytes it writes for downstream keys
  # (outside-workspace files are always keyed, never filtered);
  # trunk-tools' scopes its key to .trunk/ plus the pinned launcher binary
  # trunk-install writes. Every linter, runtime and plugin pin in trunk.yaml
  # is downloaded once and reused until a pin (or other trunk.yaml edit)
  # changes; keep the two filter lists in lockstep. The seed repo is a
  # scratch git repo so `trunk install` needs nothing else from the commit;
  # the check tasks then find the tools already installed.
  - key: trunk-config
    use: [code]
    filter:
      - .trunk/trunk.yaml
      - .trunk/configs
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      mkdir -p "$HOME/trunk-seed"
      cp -r .trunk "$HOME/trunk-seed/.trunk"
      rm -rf "$HOME/trunk-seed/.trunk/.gitignore"
      cd "$HOME/trunk-seed"
      git init -q
      # The seed commit's bytes feed trunk-tools' cache key: $HOME is
      # outside the workspace, so it is always keyed, never filtered. Pin
      # the dates so a cold-cache re-execution here writes identical bytes
      # instead of busting the downstream hit with wall-clock timestamps.
      export GIT_AUTHOR_DATE="2000-01-01T00:00:00+00:00"
      export GIT_COMMITTER_DATE="2000-01-01T00:00:00+00:00"
      git -c user.name=rwx -c user.email=rwx@example.com commit -q --allow-empty -m seed

  - key: trunk-tools
    use: [trunk-install, trunk-config]
    # Same filter as trunk-config's, and load-bearing for the same reason:
    # filters apply only to the task defining them, so without this one
    # trunk-tools would key on the whole clone and cache-miss on every
    # commit. It needs nothing else from the workspace -- the seed repo and
    # the trunk binary both live outside it.
    filter:
      - .trunk/trunk.yaml
      - .trunk/configs
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      cd "$HOME/trunk-seed"
      trunk install --ci < /dev/null

  - key: trunk-check-pr
    use: [trunk-tools, deps]
    if: ${{ init.event-type == 'pull_request' }}
    env:
      BASE_SHA: ${{ init.base-sha }}
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      # When the base branch (main) moves after a PR is created, GitHub's
      # pull_request.base.sha points to main's new tip, which may not be in
      # the PR clone. Fetch it to ensure it's available, then use merge-base
      # to find the actual fork point (stable even when main has moved).
      if ! git cat-file -e "${BASE_SHA}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
        if git fetch origin "${BASE_SHA}" 2>/dev/null; then
          : # Fetch succeeded, base SHA now available
        else
          echo "error: could not resolve base SHA ${BASE_SHA}" >&2
          exit 1
        fi
      fi
      # Compute the true fork point, not the moving tip of the base branch.
      # When main hasn't moved, merge-base equals BASE_SHA (identical behavior).
      # When main has moved, merge-base returns the actual fork point.
      MERGE_BASE="$(git merge-base HEAD "${BASE_SHA}")"
      trunk check --upstream="${MERGE_BASE}" --ci < /dev/null

  # Post-merge safety net (push to main, or manual `rwx run` dispatch): lint
  # the whole tree, not just a PR diff, so drift that slipped past incremental
  # PR runs turns main red.
  - key: trunk-check-full
    use: [trunk-tools, deps]
    if: ${{ init.event-type == 'push' }}
    run: trunk check --all --ci < /dev/null

  # Tach's external-dependency audit (the `unused_external_dependencies =
  # "error"` rule in tach.toml): fails if pyproject.toml declares a runtime
  # dependency no package file imports. Runs here as its own task because it
  # cannot be a Trunk lint command: Trunk executes batch lint commands from
  # a sandbox holding only the diff's files, and the audit decides "used"
  # from the imports visible there, so every dependency whose import sites
  # sit outside the diff got a false "not used" error (observed on #108's
  # own PR: all four runtime deps flagged, which would have rejected every
  # queue entry once the merge queue gates on the lint pipeline). Here it
  # sees the full checkout, like the drift checks in [test]. The tach pin in
  # pyproject.toml matches the trunk-managed tach@0.35.1 the module-boundary
  # lint gate uses.
  - key: tach-external
    use: [deps]
    run: uv run tach check-external
```

```yaml
  # `sdk-python-linear-trunk` vault -- never in `sdk-python-linear`, which holds

        value: ${{ vaults.sdk-python-linear-trunk.secrets.TRUNK_API_TOKEN }}
        cache-key: excluded
      TRUNK_ORG_SLUG: sanhedrin
      TRUNK_TEST_COLLECTION_ID: HJL9OODn
      CUSTOM: "true"
      JOB_URL: https://cloud.rwx.com/mint/elviskahoro/runs/${{ run.id }}
      BRANCH: ${{ init.branch }}
      PR_NUMBER: ${{ init.pr-number }}
      COMMIT_BRANCH: ${{ init.branch }}
      COMMIT_SHA: ${{ init.commit-sha }}

      trunk_launcher="$(mktemp)"

        --junit-paths "tmp/junit-*.xml" \
        --allow-empty-test-results=false \
        --org-url-slug "${TRUNK_ORG_SLUG}" \
        --use-uncloned-repo \
        --repo-url "${REPO}" \
        --repo-head-sha "${COMMIT_SHA}" \
        --repo-head-branch "${BRANCH}" \
        --repo-head-author-name rwx \
        --repo-head-commit-epoch "$(date +%s)" \

  - key: test

    run: |
      code="$(cat tmp/pytest-exit-code)"
      if [ "${code}" != "0" ]; then
        echo "pytest failed (exit ${code})" >&2
        exit "${code}"

      uv run python scripts/gen_operations.py --check

  # than in a user's traceback. Keyless by design -- no trigger needs vault

  # failure a user with a bad key sees.
  # cache: false is required, not cosmetic: the result depends on Linear's
  # live schema, not just this repo's files, so a cache hit would freeze the
  # drift check exactly when upstream moved. RWX caches tasks by content by
  # default and does not detect non-determinism (see
  # https://www.rwx.com/docs/caching).
  - key: schema-drift
    use: [deps, captain]
    cache: false
    run: captain run sdk-python-linear-pytest-network
```

### Gotchas visible in the reference files
- **Triggers:** `on.github` takes `pull_request`, `push` (a single item or a list of `- if:` items) and `status-checks: name:`. `on.cli`, `on.dispatch` and `on.cron` are also available. A manual run needs a `cli` entry.
- **Merge-queue branches:** the queue's `trunk-merge/**` branches are matched with `starts-with(event.git.branch, 'trunk-merge/')`.
- **Base image:** all files use `base: image: ubuntu:24.04` with `config: rwx/base 1.2.0`. Standard tasks are `git/clone 2.2.0`, `python/install 2.0.1`, `rwx/install-captain 1.2.0` and `github/install-cli 1.1.0`.
- **PATH:** later tasks pick up tools through `echo … >> "$RWX_ENV/PATH"`.
- **Cache keys:** `filter:` applies only to the task that defines it. Anything depending on external state needs `cache: false`. Secrets use `cache-key: excluded`.
- **`after:`:** use `after: ${{ x.succeeded || x.skipped }}`. A list form silently skips gates when an upstream task is skipped.
- **Vaults:** branch globs do not cross `/`, so grants need both `**` and `*/*`. The "Allow public repositories" toggle is UI-only.
- **Repo visibility:** both reference repos are public, so `git/clone` needs no token.

Three questions before I write the plan:

1. **Cutover staging.** Do you want two PRs, as in sdk-python-attio #76? The first adds `.rwx/` next to the GitHub workflows. The second deletes the GitHub workflows and flips `required_statuses`. A single PR is riskier. RWX triggers only fire once the config is on `main`, so the required RWX statuses would never post on the PR that introduces them, and the merge queue would stall.

2. **Workflows to keep on GitHub Actions.** `pullfrog.yml` is vendor-managed. `trunk-impacted-targets.yml` is a curl upload that needs `TRUNK_API_TOKEN`. Pick one:
   - (a) Keep pullfrog on GitHub Actions and port impacted-targets to RWX. This is what I'd pick, matching the sibling repos for pullfrog.
   - (b) Keep both on GitHub Actions.
   - (c) Port both to RWX.

3. **Repo visibility.** Is `elviskahoro/buridan-ui` public? If it is, `git/clone` needs no token. If it's private, I'll add a `github-token` from a vault.

I'd also need to know whether the RWX GitHub App is installed on the repo, and whether you want vaults created for the Trunk token. I can't check either from here.

Plan so far: port `tests.yml`, `trunk-check.yml` and `validate-assets.yml` to `.rwx/`, modeled on the sdk-python-linear files. Add an ignore for `.rwx/**` in `.trunk/trunk.yaml`, and later rename the three required statuses.

# Migrate buridan-ui CI/CD to RWX

## Context
buridan-ui runs CI on GitHub Actions (tests, trunk-check, docs/assets validation, trunk impacted-targets, pullfrog). sdk-python-attio and sdk-python-linear already moved to RWX. Repo is public (verified via `gh`), so `git/clone` needs no token. Pullfrog stays on GHA (vendor-managed); everything else moves.

## Staging (two PRs, per sdk-python-attio #76)
RWX triggers only fire from the default branch, so a required RWX status can't post on its introducing PR.
- **PR 1 (this branch):** add `.rwx/*.yml` alongside the GHA workflows; leave `required_statuses` unchanged.
- **PR 2 (after PR 1 merges and RWX runs are green on main):** delete the ported GHA workflows, flip `merge.required_statuses` in `.trunk/trunk.yaml`, update AGENTS.md lines ~25-60.

## PR 1 files
Model on `/home/vercel-sandbox/sdk-python-linear/.rwx/{lint,tests}.yml` and `sdk-python-attio/.rwx/trunk-check.yml` (base `ubuntu:24.04`, `rwx/base 1.2.0`, `git/clone 2.2.0`, checksum-pinned uv and trunk launcher, `status-checks: name:`).

1. `.rwx/tests.yml` — status name `tests`. Triggers: PR, push to main and `trunk-merge/*`, cli. Tasks: clone, uv-install, `uv sync --frozen --group dev`, `uv run pytest -q`.
2. `.rwx/trunk-check.yml` — status `trunk-check`. PR + `trunk-merge/*` push only (no push-to-main run, matching today). Tasks: clone (full depth, preserve .git), uv sync (pyright/pyrefly need `.venv`), trunk-install, trunk-config/trunk-tools cache, `trunk check --ci --upstream` using the PR base SHA merge-base (lint.yml pattern).
3. `.rwx/validate-assets.yml` — status `docs-and-assets`. Same triggers as tests. Tasks: `uv sync --group dev`, `generate_anatomy.py --check`, `generate_markdown.py`, `git diff --exit-code assets/docs` (needs preserve-git-dir), the two pytest files.
4. `.rwx/trunk-impacted-targets.yml` — PR trigger, no path filters; port the curl PUT; `TRUNK_API_TOKEN` from a new vault `buridan-ui-trunk` with `cache-key: excluded`, `cache: false`; keep the empty-token skip.
5. `.trunk/trunk.yaml` — add ignore for `.rwx/**` (gha-* rules misfire), as in the sibling repos.
6. Python version: read `.python-version` rather than hardcoding 3.13.

## Manual prerequisites (user)
- RWX GitHub App installed on elviskahoro/buridan-ui.
- Create vault `buridan-ui-trunk` with `TRUNK_API_TOKEN`; grants `elviskahoro/buridan-ui:**`, `*/*`, `:main`.

## Verification
- `rwx lint` / validate each file locally if the CLI is available; `trunk check` on the new YAML.
- After PR 1 opens: confirm RWX runs for the PR; `rwx run` (cli trigger) per file.
- PR 2: confirm RWX statuses appear on a trunk-merge queue entry before flipping required_statuses.
- Not verifiable here: live RWX runs, vault resolution.

3.11
# Uploads impacted targets for the Trunk merge queue.
#
# The queue runs in graph (Parallel) mode, where Trunk holds every PR at "Not
# Ready" until impacted targets have been uploaded for its head commit. This repo
# is a single deployable unit, so every PR declares that it impacts everything
# (impactsAllTargets): the queue then serializes entries instead of testing them
# in parallel.
#
# Authenticates with the TRUNK_API_TOKEN repo secret (a Trunk API key). The
# trunk-io/login OIDC action returned HTTP 500 for this repo, so the REST
# endpoint is called directly:
# https://docs.trunk.io/merge-queue/reference/api-v2/impactedtargets/upload-a-pull-requests-impacted-targets
#
# Fork and Dependabot PRs get no secrets, so they skip the upload with a warning
# (green check) and stay at "Not Ready" until a maintainer re-pushes the branch
# from this repo.
#
# Do NOT add path filters here: a PR that skips this workflow never uploads, and
# the queue would hold it forever. Re-uploads on every push via `synchronize`.
name: Trunk Impacted Targets

on:
  pull_request:
    branches:
      - main

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  upload-impacted-targets:
    name: Upload Impacted Targets
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Upload impacted targets
        env:
          TRUNK_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.TRUNK_API_TOKEN }}
          # Trunk's internal ID for elviskahoro/buridan-ui (not the queue ID).
          TRUNK_REPOSITORY_ID: c064fac2-557f-48fd-9979-1f94fa82cb55
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          TARGET_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
        run: |
          if [ -z "${TRUNK_API_TOKEN}" ]; then
            echo "::warning::TRUNK_API_TOKEN is unavailable (fork or Dependabot PR); skipping upload"
            exit 0
          fi
          status=$(curl -sS -o response.json -w '%{http_code}' \
            -X PUT https://api.trunk.io/v2/impacted-targets \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TRUNK_API_TOKEN}" \
            -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
            -d "{\"repositoryId\":\"${TRUNK_REPOSITORY_ID}\",\"targetBranch\":\"${TARGET_BRANCH}\",\"sha\":\"${HEAD_SHA}\",\"number\":${PR_NUMBER},\"impactsAllTargets\":true}")
          cat response.json
          [ "${status}" = "202" ] || { echo "::error::Trunk returned HTTP ${status}"; exit 1; }

UVTASK='  # Checksum-pinned uv installer: fails closed if the script at the versioned
  # URL ever changes. No packaged uv/install leaf exists in the RWX catalog.
  - key: uv-install
    use: [code]
    run: |

cat > .rwx/trunk-check.yml <<'EOF'
# Ports .github/workflows/trunk-check.yml: diff-only Trunk lint gate.
# Not path-filtered (would deadlock the Trunk Merge Queue). No push-to-main
# run, matching the GitHub workflow.
on:
  github:
    pull_request:
      init:
        commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
        lint-upstream: origin/main
      status-checks:
        name: trunk-check
    push:
      - if: ${{ starts-with(event.git.branch, 'trunk-merge/') || starts-with(event.git.branch, 'trunk-merge-beta/') }}
        init:
          commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
          lint-upstream: origin/main
        status-checks:
          name: trunk-check
  cli:
    init:
      commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
      lint-upstream: origin/main

base:
  image: ubuntu:24.04
  config: rwx/base 1.2.0

tasks:
  - key: code
    call: git/clone 2.2.0
    with:
      repository: https://github.com/elviskahoro/buridan-ui.git
      ref: ${{ init.commit-sha }}
      preserve-git-dir: true
      fetch-full-depth: true

  # Checksum-pinned uv installer: fails closed if the script changes.
  - key: uv-install
    use: [code]
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      script="$(mktemp)"
      trap 'rm -f "${script}"' EXIT
      curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/0.11.29/install.sh -o "${script}"
      echo "504a79fd2ed0dcd47e7f04f0792cfd0871f62e24a7fe40fa8ae0f563a369f2bd  ${script}" | sha256sum -c -
      sh "${script}"
      echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$RWX_ENV/PATH"

  # pyright and pyrefly resolve against .venv (see the pyright override in
  # .trunk/trunk.yaml), so the lint gate needs the project synced.
  - key: deps
    use: [uv-install]
    run: uv sync --frozen --group dev

  # Trunk launcher, checksum-pinned: trunk.io/releases/trunk is latest-only,
  # so any upstream change fails closed. Re-pin deliberately on mismatch.
  - key: trunk-install
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      trunk_launcher="$(mktemp)"
      if ! curl -fsSL https://trunk.io/releases/trunk -o "${trunk_launcher}" ||
        ! echo "700f8bbedfd226595999ea2202b9a7af75ba8398dd711f5f159f5bbba6cbf322  ${trunk_launcher}" | sha256sum -c -; then
        rm -f "${trunk_launcher}"
        echo "error: trunk launcher download or checksum failed" >&2
        exit 1
      fi
      if ! install -m 755 "${trunk_launcher}" /usr/local/bin/trunk 2>/dev/null; then
        mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/bin"
        install -m 755 "${trunk_launcher}" "$HOME/.local/bin/trunk"
        echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$RWX_ENV/PATH"
      fi
      rm -f "${trunk_launcher}"

  # Tool cache. A `filter` scopes only the task that defines it, so
  # trunk-config and trunk-tools each declare the same .trunk/ filter; keep
  # the two lists in lockstep.
  - key: trunk-config
    use: code
    filter:
      - .trunk/trunk.yaml
      - .trunk/configs
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      mkdir -p "$HOME/trunk-seed"
      cp -r .trunk "$HOME/trunk-seed/.trunk"
      rm -rf "$HOME/trunk-seed/.trunk/.gitignore"
      cd "$HOME/trunk-seed"
      git init -q
      # Pinned dates keep a cold-cache re-run byte-identical.
      export GIT_AUTHOR_DATE="2000-01-01T00:00:00+00:00"
      export GIT_COMMITTER_DATE="2000-01-01T00:00:00+00:00"
      git -c user.name=rwx -c user.email=rwx@example.com commit -q --allow-empty -m seed

  - key: trunk-tools
    use: [trunk-install, trunk-config]
    filter:
      - .trunk/trunk.yaml
      - .trunk/configs
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      cd "$HOME/trunk-seed"
      trunk install --ci < /dev/null

  - key: lint
    use: [deps, trunk-tools]
    env:
      UPSTREAM: ${{ init.lint-upstream }}
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      git fetch origin main
      # `< /dev/null` and --ci: trunk hangs on interactive prompts without a TTY.
      trunk check --ci --upstream "$UPSTREAM" < /dev/null
EOF

Review (by pi)
------------------------------------------------------------
## Review Summary

The commit adds four RWX CI pipeline definitions (`.rwx/{tests,trunk-check,validate-assets,trunk-impacted-targets}.yml`) porting the existing GitHub Actions workflows, plus a `checkov` ignore for `.rwx/**` in `.trunk/trunk.yaml` (because checkov's `gha-*` rules misfire on RWX task-level env). I verified both pinned checksums (uv 0.11.29 installer and trunk launcher) against the live downloads — both match. The ports are otherwise faithful: test/lint/asset-validation steps match the GHA step lists, queue-branch triggers are covered, the token is kept out of the cache fingerprint (`cache-key: excluded`), and the required-status cutover is correctly deferred to a follow-up PR as stated in the commit message.

### Issues

**medium** — `.rwx/trunk-check.yml:11,32,90-95` (`lint-upstream: origin/main` / `trunk check --upstream "$UPSTREAM"`)
The GHA workflow deliberately does *not* use a static base: for `pull_request` it computes `HEAD^1` on the merge ref (the fresh main tip), falling back to `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` for head checkouts, and for queue branches uses `HEAD^1`. The RWX port hardcodes `origin/main` for every trigger. On RWX the checkout is the PR head (there is no merge ref), so a PR whose branch is not based on the latest main tip is diffed against a base that is not its merge base — trunk lints files whose content changed on main since the branch point, producing spurious "new finding" failures on files the PR never touched (and for queue branches, upstream may have advanced past the stacked main tip). Concrete harm: red `trunk-check` statuses that block the merge queue for un-rebased PRs. Suggested fix: reproduce the GHA logic in the lint task — use `git rev-parse HEAD^1` when it's a queue-branch push, otherwise `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` — instead of passing `origin/main` directly.

---

**low** — `.rwx/trunk-check.yml:71` (`use: code` on the `trunk-config` task)
Every other task in this commit uses the list form (`use: [code]`, `use: [deps]`, `use: [trunk-install, trunk-config]`). If RWX only accepts a list here, this task fails to parse and `trunk-check` never runs on any PR; if bare strings are accepted, the inconsistency is purely cosmetic. Verify against the RWX schema (or the sdk-python-attio/linear references cited in the commit message) and normalize to the list form.

---

**low** — `.rwx/trunk-impacted-targets.yml:14-21` and `.rwx/tests.yml:6` / `.rwx/validate-assets.yml:6` (pull_request triggers have no branch restriction)
The GHA originals restrict `pull_request` to `branches: [main]` (and `trunk-impacted-targets.yml` exists only to feed the queue, which targets main). The RWX ports fire on PRs to any base branch: tests/assets run needlessly on PRs to feature branches, and `trunk-impacted-targets` uploads impacts with `targetBranch` set to a non-queue branch. Harm is limited to wasted runs and possible API rejections/noise, but if RWX's `on.github.pull_request` supports a branch filter, adding one preserves parity and avoids the extra uploads.

------------------------------------------------------------
## Review Summary

The commit addresses two findings from the previous review of `.rwx/trunk-check.yml`. First, it replaces the static `lint-upstream: origin/main` init parameter with an `event-type` marker, and the `lint` task now computes the base the way the GitHub workflow does: queue-branch pushes (`trunk-merge*`) diff against `HEAD^1` (the stacked main tip), while PR/CLI runs diff against `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` (the true fork point). Second, it normalizes `use: code` to `use: [code]` on the `trunk-config` task, fixing the list-form inconsistency. I verified the shell logic against `.github/workflows/trunk-check.yml`: the push path is an exact match; the PR path intentionally substitutes `merge-base` for the merge-ref `HEAD^1` that GitHub Actions uses, since the RWX checkout is the PR head and has no merge commit. That substitution fixes the dominant failure mode flagged previously (spurious findings in files the PR never touched) but leaves a narrower divergence on overlapping files, noted below.

### Issues

**medium** — `.rwx/trunk-check.yml:111-117` (comment "Same bases as the GitHub workflow"; PR path `upstream="$(git merge-base HEAD origin/main)"`)
For the normal `pull_request` case, the GitHub workflow (`.github/workflows/trunk-check.yml`, "Trunk check (PR…)" step) lints against `HEAD^1` on the merge ref — the **fresh main tip** — not the merge base. The two differ when a PR modifies a file that main also changed since the branch point: with the merge-ref base, main's own hunks are the first parent of the diff and any lint finding main introduced in that file is excluded; with the merge-base base, the diff `merge-base..HEAD` includes main's change to that file, so a finding introduced **on main** is counted as "new" and fails the PR's `trunk-check` even though the PR author didn't introduce it. Concretely: PR touches `foo.ts`, main also landed a change to `foo.ts` after the PR branched, main's change has a lint finding → red `trunk-check` on the RWX pipeline where the GHA pipeline passes. The author recovers by rebasing (which moves the merge base to the new main tip), so it's a spurious-failure annoyance rather than a security/data issue, but the in-file comment claiming "Same bases as the GitHub workflow" overstates parity. Suggested fix: either replicate the merge ref locally (e.g., attempt `git merge --no-commit --no-ff origin/main` and use `HEAD^1`, falling back to `merge-base` when the merge conflicts), or correct the comment to document the residual divergence and that rebasing resolves it.

---

**low** — `.rwx/trunk-check.yml:116` (PR path does not verify `origin/main` is an ancestor of HEAD)
`git merge-base HEAD origin/main` still succeeds and yields the old fork point if the PR contains a squashed/cherry-picked copy of main's history where `origin/main` is not an ancestor — an unusual-but-possible state after upstream force-pushes or odd rebases. Harm is limited to an overly large diff fed to `trunk check --upstream`, producing the same class of spurious "new finding" failures described above. Adding a guard (e.g., `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD || echo "warning: origin/main not an ancestor; diff may include main drift" >&2`) would make the failure mode diagnosable instead of mysterious. Low priority since the clone is full-depth and the branch protection rules make non-ancestor states rare.

126	```
127	
128	- **Default to one commit per PR.** Multi-commit PRs are only OK when each commit is independently reviewable and the slices land in order.
129	- Squash with `git rebase -i main` or `git reset --soft main && git commit`. Never use `--no-edit` flags that bypass message review.
130	- The squashed commit message mirrors the PR title's intent (sentence-cased, why-focused) and captures the motivation in the body. No Conventional Commits prefix.
131	- If the branch already has a single commit (or each existing commit is independently reviewable and ordered), skip the rebase but still confirm the count before moving on.
132	- **Never force-push to a shared branch to squash after publication.** Squash *before* the first push.
133	
134	### Step 5: Run relevant tests locally, then roborev review before drafting
135	
136	**Roborev reviews the diff; it does not execute the test suite.** A clean roborev pass says nothing about whether the code runs — it has caught logic/quality issues while a hardcoded assertion in a test file was still broken. Before roborev, run whatever tests cover the changed files:
137	
138	- Identify affected tests by mirroring the changed path under `tests/` (many repos mirror source layout — a change to `pkg/foo.py` often has a matching `tests/.../test_foo.py`) and/or `grep -rn` the changed file's distinctive strings (a literal like an `if:` condition, a flag name) across `tests/` to catch assertions on exact values.
139	- Run the narrowest test target that covers the change (in a uv-based Python repo, `uv run pytest tests/<mirrored-path>`; otherwise the repo's own test command) — full-suite runs are fine too, but don't skip this step because CI will "catch it anyway": local runs take seconds, CI takes minutes.
140	- If a test fails, fix it now and fold the fix into the same commit (Step 3/4), *before* running roborev — don't push and let CI discover it.
141	
142	**Hard gate: do not draft the PR or move toward `git push` until roborev has run and either reported clean or been explicitly acknowledged by the user.** This applies even if the change feels trivial, even if the diff is one line, and even if the user has not asked for review explicitly — the skill always runs roborev before the user is asked to approve a draft.
143	
144	With the squashed commit in place but the branch still local, run a local AI code review with roborev so findings surface *before* the user sees a draft and *before* GitHub sees the diff. Invoke the `roborev` executable directly with the `--wait` flag; Git aliases are optional conveniences and may not exist in cloud sandboxes:
145	
146	```bash
147	roborev review --wait
148	```
149	
150	- `--wait` is **required**, not optional — it blocks until the review completes so findings are available before the draft is shown. Do not run `roborev review` without `--wait`.
151	- A bare `roborev review` — or a leftover post-commit auto-review hook — only **enqueues a background daemon job and returns before a verdict exists**. An enqueue is not a pass: if HEAD already has a queued or running background review, block on it (`roborev review --wait`, or `roborev wait` for the already-enqueued job) so an actual verdict is in hand before drafting. Never report "review enqueued" or a missing verdict as clean.
152	- Capture the outcome (clean, N findings fixed in M rounds, N findings unresolved, unavailable) — Step 8 surfaces it inside the draft preview so the user can see the gate was walked.
153	- **Review loop (no permission prompts):** if roborev surfaces findings, fix them yourself without asking — **every severity counts**, including low and nit. Do not stop, summarize, or ask "fix these?" / "defer or proceed?" because findings are low severity. Fix as many as possible that are small in scope: a wording or error-message change, a missing test case, a missing guard, a rename, a local refactor inside the changed function. Do not fix findings that would reshape the surrounding design, change public interfaces, or touch files outside this PR's scope; for those only, report them to the user with the reason they were not fixed. Put the fixes in a follow-up commit, re-squash (Step 4), and re-run `roborev review --wait` (this step). Repeat until a run comes back clean or only out-of-scope findings remain. Do not ask "fix and rerun?" — that is the default action.
154	- **Loop cap:** stop after 3 fix rounds. If findings remain, or a finding would need a product or design decision rather than a code fix, stop looping and list the unresolved findings in the Step 8 draft preview, so the user decides at the single approval gate. Never amend or force-push past findings silently.
155	- If roborev is unavailable (command not installed, no network), say so explicitly to the user and ask whether to proceed without review. Do not silently skip.
156	- For deeper fix/refine loops, consult the repo's roborev guide skill if it ships one.
157	
158	### Step 6: Draft the title
159	
160	The title is a formal, sentence-cased statement of **why this change exists** — not a conventional commit subject. A reviewer scanning the PR list should understand the *motivation*, not just the area of code touched.
161	
162	Rules:
163	
164	- **Formal, sentence case.** "Eliminate duplicated Attio retry logic across five call sites" — not "attio retry refactor".
165	- **Lead with the why, not the what.** Prefer the problem solved or the outcome enabled over the mechanical change. "Unblock Linear → Attio sync from rate-limit drift" beats "Add retry decorator to Attio client".
166	- **No Conventional Commits prefix.** Do **not** use `feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, etc. Even if recent commits or PRs use them, PR titles in this ecosystem are full sentences. Commit messages and PR titles are different surfaces.
167	- **Under 70 characters where possible**, but clarity wins over brevity — GitHub truncates in list views, so front-load the most important words.
168	- **Specific.** "Fix off-by-one in Apollo pagination cursor causing missed contacts" — not "Bug fix" or "Improvements".
169	- **No ticket IDs in the title.** They go in Links.
170	- **No trailing period.**
171	- **Avoid bare imperative verbs** like "Add", "Fix", "Update" as the first word when a why-framing is possible. They're allowed when the why genuinely is the action (e.g., a clear bugfix), but check first whether the motivation can lead instead.
172	
173	Good vs. bad title shapes:
174	
175	| Bad (conventional / what-focused) | Good (formal / why-focused) |
176	| --- | --- |
177	| `feat: add retry decorator` | `Consolidate Attio retry logic to unblock Linear sync` |
178	| `fix: pagination bug` | `Fix off-by-one in Apollo pagination cursor causing missed contacts` |
179	| `refactor: clean up attio client` | `Eliminate divergent retry behavior across Attio call sites` |
180	| `chore: bump deps` | `Bump httpx to 0.27 to pick up the connection-pool leak fix` |
181	
182	### Step 7: Draft the description
183	
184	Use this template. **Drop sections that have nothing meaningful in them** — a section containing "None" or "N/A" is worse than no section.
185	
186	```markdown
187	## Why
188	<1-3 paragraphs. Lead with the problem or constraint. State the motivation. Reference upstream context (ticket, spec) by link, not paraphrase. The reviewer should finish this section understanding what would happen if the PR were *not* merged.>
189	
190	## Trade-offs
191	<Only if there were meaningful alternatives. Format: "Chose X over Y because Z." Skip if the approach was obvious or there was only one reasonable way.>
192	
193	## Risks
194	<What could break that isn't already covered by tests. Note rollback path if non-trivial. Skip for clearly low-risk changes (docs, comments, isolated refactors with full coverage).>
195	
196	## Test plan
197	<Reasoning, not output. "Exercised X path with Y inputs because Z is the highest-risk surface." If full unit coverage exists and the change is small/obvious, skip this section.>
198	
199	## Links
200	- Linear: [TEAM-NNN](https://linear.app/...)
201	- Spec: design/backlog-...-spec-01.md
202	- Plan: design/backlog-...-plan-01.md
203	- Related PRs: #NNN
204	- Closes #NNN (only when Step 2 confirmed this PR fully resolves a same-repo GitHub issue)
205	```
206	
207	Section guidance:
208	
209	| Section | Required? | When to drop it |
210	| --- | --- | --- |
211	| Why | Always | Never. If you can't write a specific one, the work isn't ready. |
212	| Trade-offs | When meaningful alternatives existed | Obvious one-way changes, fixes to clear bugs |
213	| Risks | When the change has non-trivial blast radius | Docs, comments, isolated refactors with coverage |
214	| Test plan | When testing required judgment calls | Small changes with full unit coverage |
215	| Links | If any upstream artifact exists | True greenfield work with no ticket, spec, or predecessor PR |
216	
217	### Step 8: Show the draft. Wait for confirmation. (Single approval gate before push.)
218	
219	**This is the only user-approval gate in the workflow, and it sits immediately before `git push`.** Steps 3–5 (commit, squash, roborev) must already be complete by the time you reach it — by construction the agent cannot honor a "yes" without having walked the roborev gate first.
220	
221	Show the draft title, the draft body, **and the roborev outcome** so the user can see the gate was walked. Even if the user said "create a PR", they agreed to the action, not blind-trusted your draft.
222	
223	**Shortcut:** If the user re-sends this *exact* create_pr prompt verbatim, or an explicit approval phrase like "create/open the PR now," immediately after the agent has already shown a draft under this step, treat that as the Step 8 approval — proceed exactly as a "yes" would (Steps 9–13), don't re-run Steps 1–7 to produce a fresh draft. Anything else — a revision request, a question about the draft, or a paraphrase — is not the shortcut; treat it as normal feedback and re-show the draft.
224	
225	Format the preview as:
226	
227	```text
228	Title: <draft title>
229	
230	Body:
231	---
232	<draft body>
233	---
234	
235	Roborev: <clean (after M fix rounds) | N findings unresolved (list them) | unavailable (reason)>
236	
237	Push and create this PR? (or edit before I submit)
238	```
239	
240	The roborev line is mandatory — never omit it. If it shows "unavailable", the user is implicitly being asked to proceed without review.
241	
242	If the user requests edits, revise and re-show. Don't auto-submit. A "yes" here authorizes closing or linking the GitHub issue (Step 9), the rebase (Step 10), the push (Step 11), and the PR creation (Step 12) — proceed through all of them without re-prompting (pausing only if the rebase hits conflicts).
243	
244	### Step 9: Note the GitHub issue disposition
245	
246	If Step 2 identified a GitHub issue this PR addresses, carry its disposition forward — the actual action happens in Step 12b, once a PR URL exists:
247	
248	- **Same-repo issue, fully resolved by this PR** — the `Closes #NNN` line already lives in the PR body (Step 7's Links section). Nothing further is needed here: GitHub auto-closes the issue when the PR merges into `main`. Don't `gh issue close` it now — the fix isn't on `main` yet.
249	- **Cross-repo issue, or only partially resolved** — GitHub's closing keywords don't work across repos and shouldn't be used for partial work. Remember to leave a linking comment in Step 12b instead of closing it.
250	- **Ambiguous whether this PR fully resolves it** — this should already have been resolved in Step 2; if it wasn't, ask the user now rather than guessing at merge-closing behavior.
251	- Skip silently if no GitHub issue was identified in Step 2.
252	- Already authorized by the Step 8 "yes" — don't re-prompt.
253	
254	### Step 10: Rebase onto the latest base (last step before opening the PR)
255	
256	**This is the final step before the PR is opened.** Immediately before pushing, rebase the branch onto the freshest base so the PR opens against current `main` and merge conflicts surface here — locally, where they're cheap to resolve — instead of in GitHub's merge UI.
257	
258	This must happen **before** the first push (Step 11), not after. Rebasing a branch that's already on `origin` would require a force-push, which is forbidden without explicit user approval.
259	
260	```bash
261	git fetch origin
262	git rebase origin/main   # or the confirmed base branch from pre-flight
263	```
264	
265	- If the rebase is clean, proceed to Step 11.
266	- If the rebase hits conflicts, **stop and surface them to the user.** Resolve them (or have the user resolve them), then re-run Steps 4–5 (re-squash if needed, re-run `roborev review --wait`) so the review reflects the rebased history. Never `git rebase --skip` or abandon conflicting hunks silently.
267	- If the branch is already up to date with the base, the rebase is a no-op — proceed.
268	
269	### Step 11: Push the branch
270	
271	Once the rebase is clean, push the branch to `origin` with upstream tracking.
272	
273	```bash
274	git push -u origin "$(git branch --show-current)"
275	```
276	
277	Confirm the push succeeded before moving on. If it fails (auth, protected branch, non-fast-forward), surface the error and stop — do not force-push.
278	
279	### Step 12: Create the PR
280	
281	**Hard gate before running `gh pr create`: for every same-repo GitHub issue Step 2 determined this PR fully resolves, mechanically verify the drafted body contains a `Closes #NNN` / `Fixes #NNN` / `Resolves #NNN` line for *that specific* issue number before shelling out — one PR can fully resolve more than one issue, and each needs its own closing reference, not just the first.** This is a real known failure mode, not a hypothetical: gtm-sdk#609 was fully fixed by gtm-sdk#628, but the drafted body only listed "gtm-sdk#609" under Links without a closing keyword, so GitHub never auto-closed it and it sat open until manually closed later. A "the plan said to add it" belief is not sufficient — grep the actual string you're about to pass to `--body` for the pattern before running the command, once per fully-resolved issue number:
282	
283	```bash
284	grep -qiE "(closes|fixes|resolves) #${ISSUE_NUMBER}([^[:alnum:]_]|$)" <<< "$PR_BODY"
285	```
286	
287	`\b` is not portable to the BSD `grep` on macOS — use the `([^[:alnum:]_]|$)` form above instead, which matches the same "word boundary or end of string" intent on both BSD and GNU grep.
288	
289	If that grep fails for any fully-resolved issue number, **stop and fix the body** — don't proceed to `gh pr create` with a body that silently downgraded to a bare reference. If Step 2 flagged partial/cross-repo instead, the grep is expected to fail and that's correct — don't add the keyword in that case.
290	
291	To make this checkable, assign the HEREDOC to `PR_BODY` first, grep that exact variable, then pass it to `--body` — don't construct the body inline in the `gh pr create` call, since there's nothing to grep before shelling out:
292	
293	```bash
294	PR_BODY="$(cat <<'EOF'
295	## Why
296	... (real newlines, not \n)
297	EOF
298	)"
299	
300	for ISSUE_NUMBER in "${FULLY_RESOLVED_ISSUE_NUMBERS[@]}"; do  # every issue Step 2 flagged as fully resolved
301	  grep -qiE "(closes|fixes|resolves) #${ISSUE_NUMBER}([^[:alnum:]_]|$)" <<< "$PR_BODY" || {
302	    echo "missing closing keyword for #${ISSUE_NUMBER}" >&2
303	    exit 1
304	  }
305	done
306	
307	gh pr create --title "Fix race in Apollo enrichment dedup that double-charged credits" --body "$PR_BODY"
308	```
309	
310	Return the PR URL to the user. Don't add follow-up commentary unless the user asks — the URL is the work product.
311	
312	### Step 12b: Link the GitHub issue, if Step 9 deferred it
313	
314	Only applies when Step 9 flagged a **cross-repo or partially-resolved** issue — the fully-resolved same-repo case already carries its `Closes #NNN` in the PR body and needs no action here.
315	
316	```bash
317	gh issue comment <number> --body "Addressed in <PR URL from Step 12>"                    # same-repo, partial
318	gh issue comment <number> --repo <owner/repo> --body "Addressed in <PR URL from Step 12>" # cross-repo — use the owner/repo saved in Step 2
319	```
320	
321	- `<PR URL>` is the output from Step 12 — this step cannot run before Step 12 for exactly that reason.
322	- Do not close the issue yourself; partial or cross-repo work isn't the maintainer's signal to close it.
323	- Skip silently if Step 9 found nothing to do here.
324	
325	### Step 13: Suggest the merge once tests and checks pass
326	
327	Merging is never automatic. Once the PR is open, check its status with a single call (`gh pr checks <pr-number>`). When tests and required checks have passed, suggest merging with the GitHub CLI and wait for the user to say yes:
328	
329	```bash
330	gh pr merge <pr-number> --squash
331	```
332	
333	- Do not poll in a loop. If checks are still running, report that and stop; the user can ask again later.
334	- Do not log in to, configure, or call any merge-queue service. If `gh` is not authenticated, say so and stop.
335	- Never pass `--admin` or `--auto` unless the user asks for it.
336	
337	## Modifiers: drafts, reviewers, labels
338	
339	`gh pr create` accepts modifiers that don't affect the description but matter for the PR's lifecycle. Don't auto-set any of these; only pass what the user explicitly asks for:
340	
341	| Flag | When |
342	| --- | --- |
343	| `--draft` | User says "draft", or commit history shows clear in-progress markers ("WIP", "spike"). |
344	| `--reviewer <handle>` | Only when the user names reviewers. Don't guess. |
345	| `--label <name>` | Only labels that exist (`gh label list`). Invented labels silently no-op. |
346	| `--assignee <handle>` | Default to `@me` unless told otherwise. |
347	| `--base <branch>` | Only override the default branch when the user says so. |
348	
349	## Anti-patterns
350	
351	These show up in autogenerated PR descriptions and this skill must actively avoid them. Several come from defaults baked into other tools — including the default `gh pr create` template suggested by the Bash tool — and this skill overrides them.
352	
353	### Don't summarize the diff
354	
355	```markdown
356	## Summary
357	- Added `retry_with_backoff` helper in `apollo/client.py`
358	- Updated `enrich_account` to use it
359	- Added 3 unit tests in `test_apollo.py`
360	```
361	
362	The reviewer is about to read the diff. This is duplicate work that rots the moment the diff changes. Replace with **Why**.
363	
364	### Don't write empty sections
365	
366	```markdown
367	## Risks
368	None.
369	
370	## Test plan
371	Tested locally.
372	```
373	
374	"None" and "Tested locally" carry zero signal. Drop the section.
375	
376	### Don't add AI attribution
377	
378	The repo's agent instructions (AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md) prohibit AI attribution in commits and PRs.
379	**Never** emit:
380	
381	- `Co-Authored-By: Claude <claude@anthropic.com>`
382	- `🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](...)`
383	- Any "Generated by ..." or "Powered by ..." footer
384	
385	The Bash tool's default PR template includes the 🤖 footer. **Strip it.** This skill overrides that default.
386	
387	### Don't restate the title
388	
389	If the title is "Fix race in Apollo enrichment dedup", the description shouldn't open with "This PR fixes a race in the Apollo enrichment dedup logic." Start the Why with the problem, not a rephrase.
390	
391	### Don't pad with boilerplate
392	
393	- "This PR makes some improvements to ..."
394	- "As discussed offline, ..."
395	- "Cleaning up some technical debt ..."
396	
397	If you can't write a specific Why, pause and ask the user. Vague motivation is a tell that the work isn't ready for review.
398	
399	### Don't paste test output
400	
401	The Test plan section is about the *reasoning* behind what was tested. A reviewer can run the tests. They cannot rederive your reasoning from the output.
402	
403	### Don't include "Closes #NNN" without confirming
404	
405	GitHub auto-closes referenced issues on merge. Only use `Closes` / `Fixes` / `Resolves` keywords if Step 2 confirmed the PR fully resolves a **same-repo** issue. For partial work or a cross-repo issue, mention it in Links instead and leave a linking comment on the issue in Step 12b — no magic keyword. Skipping the confirmation in Step 2 is a bug, not a safe default: it leaves the issue open with no trace back to the PR that addressed it.
406	
407	### Don't autopilot the PR submission
408	
409	Even if the user said "create a PR for this", they agreed to the action, not to a specific draft. Show the draft, wait for confirmation, then submit.

412	
413	### Example 1: Small bug fix — Why + Links only
414	
415	**Title:** `Fix off-by-one in Apollo pagination cursor causing missed contacts`
416	
417	**Body:**
418	
419	```markdown
420	## Why
421	The Apollo `search_people` paginator was dropping the last page of results because the cursor check used `>` instead of `>=`. Affected every batch where total results were an exact multiple of page_size — roughly 10% of runs. Caught when a TAM build was missing ~50 known contacts ([AI-1234](https://linear.app/...)).
422	
423	## Links
424	- Linear: [AI-1234](https://linear.app/...)
425	```

427	(Trade-offs, Risks, Test plan dropped — small obvious fix, full coverage exists.)
428	
429	### Example 2: Refactor — Why + Trade-offs + Risks + Links
430	
431	**Title:** `Consolidate Attio retry logic to unblock Linear → Attio sync`
432	
433	**Body:**
434	
435	```markdown
436	## Why
437	Five call sites in `libs/attio/` were duplicating retry/backoff logic, and each had drifted: `update_person` retried on 5xx but not 429; `create_person` retried on 429 but with no backoff; `list_workspaces` did no retry at all. The new Linear → Attio sync was about to become the sixth divergent copy.
438	
439	Pulling the logic into `@retry_with_backoff` lets callers opt in with one line and ensures consistent behavior across all Attio writes.
440	
441	## Trade-offs
442	Considered `tenacity` instead. Rejected because the call sites already have idiosyncratic logic — custom backoff that respects Attio's `Retry-After` header — that `tenacity` would require a custom wait strategy to express. The hand-rolled decorator is ~30 lines and stays close to the Attio-specific behavior.
443	
444	## Risks
445	Changes the *shape* of exceptions that bubble up: `AttioRateLimit` is now wrapped in `RetryExhausted` after N attempts. Two existing callers caught `AttioRateLimit` directly; both updated in this PR. Grep for `AttioRateLimit` returns no other matches.
446	
447	## Links
448	- Linear: [AI-2891](https://linear.app/...)
449	- Spec: design/backlog-202604010000-attio_retry_decorator-spec-01.md
450	```
451

453	
454	**Bad:**
455

457	## Summary
458	- Added retry decorator
459	- Updated 5 Attio call sites
460	- Removed duplicate retry code
461	- Added tests
462	
463	## Test plan
464	- [x] Ran tests
465	- [x] Tested locally
466	
467	🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
